visuals.caption: A right triangle. The small square marks the right angle. θ marks one acute angle: the side across from θ is its opposite side, the side that touches both θ and the right angle is its adjacent side, and the longest side is the hypotenuse. Here θ is the angle of elevation: it opens upward from the horizontal ground.

A right triangle. The small square marks the right angle. θ marks one acute angle: the side across from θ is its opposite side, the side that touches both θ and the right angle is its adjacent side, and the longest side is the hypotenuse. The horizontal line of sight from the top is parallel to the ground, so θ at the bottom has the same size as the angle of depression.

A 45-45-90 triangle with legs 4 has hypotenuse 4√2: the hypotenuse is the leg times √2.
A 30-60-90 triangle with short leg 3 has long leg 3√3 and hypotenuse 6: the long leg is the short leg times √3, and the hypotenuse is twice the short leg.
Two sides 4 and 5 with a 30° included angle give the exact area 5.
Two sides 4 and 5 with a 60° included angle give the exact area 5√3.
Two sides 4 and 5 with an obtuse 120° included angle give the exact area 5√3.
